title: Learned breast-cancer feature selection nominates survival-associated transcripts
summary: Random-forest recursive feature elimination and XGBoost analysis of breast-cancer expression data nominated genes subsequently associated with distant-metastasis-free survival in a basal breast-cancer subgroup. Higher POU2AF1 and S100B expression was associated with longer survival in the reported analysis. These are exploratory expression–outcome associations, not causal mechanisms or a clinically validated prognostic test.
organization: International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology; Regional Centre for Biotechnology

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and scoped computational/clinical model Methods and corresponding Results; no operational laboratory protocols evaluated

evidence.tested: The source pooled 1,150 expression samples, including 623 triple-negative cases, to learn subtype-discriminating gene sets. Genes passing further differential-expression filtering were examined with KM Plotter and Cox analysis for distant-metastasis-free survival.
evidence.unknown: External subtype classification helped choose the final gene sets and is not an untouched evaluation of survival prognosis. Survival analysis used a St Gallen basal-subtype definition; exact survival sample counts, cutoff selection, overlap with discovery samples and multiplicity control are not fully resolved in the inspected main text. Whole-data batch adjustment and unclear feature-selection nesting can inflate classification performance, so those metrics are not the represented finding. CT83 p=.052 is not treated as significant. No perturbation or clinical-treatment effect is established.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted random-forest feature elimination and boosted-tree classification narrow the candidate transcript sets before the scoped posthoc clinical-outcome association analysis.
